title: Determining Levels of Detail for Simulators of Parallel and Distributed Computing Systems via Automated Calibration
problem: Simulator accuracy depends on level of detail AND parameter calibration; trade-off between accuracy and complexity
motivation: Manual simulator design choices difficult; need automated approach for appropriate abstraction level selection
method: The method automates the traditionally manual task of tuning a simulator: it tests the simulator with different detail levels and parameter settings, measures how each matches real-world behavior, and automatically identifies the best trade-off between accuracy and speed. A framework then systematically determines which simulator components require high detail and which can be safely simplified. Two case studies demonstrate the approach on different types of parallel and distributed systems.
key_novelty: The core innovation is an automated framework that determines the right level of detail for simulators, working across different parallel and distributed computing domains.
